"It is quite all right. It is the sort of thing that ought to have been told before, and I can see how it would sound as though it had."

aldric_return_sorry.text: "You do not," Aldric says. "Or you may; I have not decided, and it would not be the useful thing in any case." He puts the roll of linen away. "I did not leave over a discourtesy. Sit down, and I will ask you two questions, and if you answer them truthfully I will fetch my bag."

aldric_return_ask.text:
"The first is the one I asked at a fire and did not get answered." He folds his hands. "Why did you keep me?"

He waits, and he will wait, and there is no version of him that is going to help you with it.

choices.label: Because you kept everybody standing, and it meant I did not have to think about it.
Because you were the best of us.

aldric_return_one_flattery.text: "No," Aldric says, without heat. "I was not, and you have watched me be wrong in front of you at least three times. If you are going to hand me that we shall be here all night, and I have a boy with a burn coming back at the hour." He waits. "Again."

aldric_return_one_liked.text: "That may even be true," Aldric says. "It is not an answer to the question I asked, and that is not a thing that happens to me by accident." He waits. "Again."

aldric_return_one_true.text:
Aldric is quiet a moment.

"Yes," he says. "Thank you. That is what I took it to be, and I have found the last weeks a good deal harder for not being certain of it." He shifts the stool. "It is not a wound. A man who does a thing well is used for it, and I have been used for it in better houses than yours."

He looks up.

"The second question is the one that matters."

aldric_return_two.text:
"You will do it again," Aldric says. "Whatever it was — and I am not going to name it for you, because a man who names your fault has decided what it is going to be. You will do it again."

He leans forward.

"So tell me what you will do the next time. And do not tell me you will do better."

choices.label: The same thing. And I would rather you were standing there when I did it.
I will do better. You have my word.

aldric_return_two_promise.text: "No," Aldric says. "I have had that from a prior, and from a woman with a seal, and from myself, in a chapel, out loud, and not one of the three of us kept it." He is not angry. He is extremely tired. "I am not asking you to be better. I am asking you to be accurate. Again."

aldric_return_two_true.text:
"There," Aldric says, and something in him puts itself down. "That I can work with. I cannot mend a man who intends to be different tomorrow; there is nothing to take hold of."

He gets up and fetches the bag from under the bench, where it has been packed for eleven days, which he does not remark on and neither should you.

"Understand me," he says at the door. "I am not forgiven and neither are you. I have simply worked out that I would rather be in the room. It is what I have always said, and it turns out to be a great deal easier to say about strangers."

aldric_return_two_unknown.text:
"You do not know," Aldric repeats, and turns it over. "That is at least a survey and not a promise."

He gets up and fetches the bag from under the bench, where it has been packed for eleven days.

"I should have preferred the other answer," he says. "I will take this one. Understand that I am not forgiven and neither are you. I have simply worked out that I would rather be in the room."

aldric_close.text: "May I say a thing badly," Aldric says, "and would you let me finish it before you are kind about it, because the kindness is what stops me."

Aldric has been holding the same strap for some minutes without doing anything to it. "I have a sentence," he says, when he sees you see. "I have had it since the ford. It is a perfectly ordinary sentence and I have taken it apart four times to check."

choices.label: Put it back together and say it.

aldric_close.text: "I was taught that a man who wants a thing very much should hand the deciding to somebody steadier," Aldric says, to the fire. "I have come round to thinking that is an excellent rule for medicine and a cowardly one for everything else, and it has taken me eleven years."
Aldric folds the thought away with the bandage roll, unhurried. "It will keep," he says. "Most true things do."

romance_after.text: Aldric keeps the hours still — vigil to prime, the old order of it — but he has moved the keeping of them to your side of the fire, and holds the book so the light of it falls partly on you. He has not remarked on this. He is not going to.

"I have been asked what I am smiling about twice today," Aldric says, aggrieved, as if the cause were not sitting directly beside him. "Once by the ferryman. I told him it was the weather. It has been raining since Tuesday."

The pack sits where it was moved, that six inches nearer, and has stayed there through four camps and a river crossing. For a man who spent eleven years keeping his whole life strapped and liftable, six settled inches is a psalm.
Aldric shifts along the log, unasked, and goes on with the hours from there.

camp_aldric_fate.text: "I said it out loud in a guardroom," Aldric says. "Eleven years of carrying it, and the saying took under a minute, and the captain wrote three lines and dated them." He turns a bandage roll over in his hands, finds nothing wrong with it, puts it down. "I keep waiting to feel lighter. What I feel is accurate. I recommend it anyway."

"I folded it back up," Aldric says, before you have the question in order. "You were there. I am not going to pretend it was somebody else's folding." He works on in the firelight for a while. "It keeps, folded. That is the property of paper I know best. It keeps, and it waits, and it does not get lighter."
